acknowledged.detail: Backlot serves it; the real API's answer has no such field
acknowledged.note: The real API serves `edited` on a message that has been edited and on no other. `docs.slack.dev/reference/events/message` documents it: "If the message has been edited after posting, it will include an `edited` property, which includes the user ID of the editor and the timestamp for when the edit occurred." Measured 2026-09-22, no message in any of the eight channels this probe's caller can read carries one, so the vendor's half of the run had nothing to pair with the probe corpus's edited message. A field served conditionally cannot be told apart from one never served by a single caller's sample, which is why this comparison's `extra_field` findings are verified by hand like every other `extra_*`.

acknowledged.note: Real echoes the caller's credential back. Measured 2026-09-22: `api.test` carrying an `Authorization: Bearer` header answers `args: {"token": "<the token>"}`, and with `?foo=bar` beside it answers both keys; carrying no credential at all it answers `args: {}`. Backlot echoes the query and form parameters it was sent and never the header, so the key is absent. Serving it would mean writing a caller's token into a response body, which is a decision about what a mock should reproduce rather than a shape that is missing by oversight.
